title: Sitting in at the entertainment club and replacing Willie Foster with Fate Marable
summary: Musicians gather at an entertainment club; Marable, hearing him and urged by trumpeter Albert Snyder and his brother who works the boat, auditions him and hires him on banjo.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yeah, closer to the river, that's right. Yeah, I believe it was the Beverly Garden. Well, anyhow, when, after they let us off, well, that particular time, I used to do this, you'd get a place to call the entertainment club. Well, all the musicians used to hang around there and we used to go down there and, like if we had a job, we'd go sit in with the band and, you know, jam session. And, um, Faith Marvel band, all the band used to hang around there when they'd get off in their wake, you know, and, well, I had to change musicians to go around there to make yourself known and be seen, you see. And, um, Faith was, um, had an idea, he was, he was going to change banjo and he was using, uh, the Willie Forrestone banjo. And, uh, he had heard me in and I had a brother, my brother was working out on the boat, uh, not as a musician, but as a deckhand or pole or something like that. And he had been telling him about me, you know. So, uh, Faith one morning come down there and I made it, just pay attention to me and I heard me playing everything. And, well, that time, numbers like that, if you could play like the world waiting for the sunrise, if you could play Tiger Rag on the banjo or any number that you could feature on the banjo those days, you know, you would consider. And I always, like a guy, always kept up what was going on, you see. So, um, he heard me and he said, well, I want you to come out to rehearsal. He said, if you can mess. I heard about your reading and everything. He said, I, uh, I would like to get you, uh, there was a fellow on the trumpet player named Albert Snyder. He was on the boat and he spoke for me, see. Well, they knew about my reading, see. So, I, I went out to the rehearsal and, and I must have did good because, uh, next thing I think the next week or so they had me in the banjo, see. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
